title: Introduction to Express
idea: Express is a small web framework on top of Node's `http` module. It routes each request to your function and gives you helpers to answer.

analogy.text: A phone switchboard. The operator hears which extension a caller wants and connects the call to that desk. An unknown extension gets a refusal.
analogy.breaks: Extensions are fixed numbers; Express paths can contain parameters like `:id`.

points: An Express app is one function that Node's `http` server calls for every request.
A route pairs a method and a path pattern with a handler: `app.get('/books', fn)`.
A handler gets the request, `req`, and the response, `res`, with helpers like `res.json()`.
Middleware, added with `app.use`, is a function that runs before the routes below it.

hero.title: Plain http versus Express

left.title: Node's built-in http module
items: Set the content type and call `JSON.stringify` yourself
Collect the body in chunks, then parse it
Write your own reply for unknown paths

right.title: Express
items: `res.json(data)` sets the type and sends the body
Unmatched requests get a 404 reply automatically

hero.verdict: Same server underneath, less repeated code: Express handles the routine parts.

code.title: Middleware, a route, a 404
code.caption: A logger, one route and an unknown path. Press Run for the real output.

walk.text: Middleware: log every request, then `next()` passes it on.
A route. `req.params.name` reads the path; `res.json` sends the reply.
Listen on a free port (0) and build the base URL.
Request two paths. `/nope` has no route, so Express answers 404 itself.
Close the server so the script can exit.

pitfalls: Express 4 tutorials can break on Express 5: `app.get('*')` now throws at startup.
Routes match in the order you write them: put `/books/new` before `/books/:id`.
Express's default 404 is an HTML page; an API should send JSON errors instead.

quiz.why: Routes are tried in order. `/books/:id` matches `/books/new` first, with `id` set to `new`, so its handler answers.

takeaway: Express tries middleware and routes in the order added; no match means 404.
